full_judgment: 2. The suit char-land comprising Rupapura Sonapura Mouza bearing Revenue Survey No. 1547 originally appertained to Touzi No. 1566 of Noakhali Collectorate. It was transferred to Bakerganj Collectorate in the year 1965. The Char-land was in existence from before 1860 and upto 1894 when it went into the river. It reappeared and reformed in situ in the year 1947-48. As a great number of river claimants were about to take forcible possession of the land, the Collector of Bakerganj attached it and made a reference to the Civil Court under Section 5(1) of the Bengal Alluvial Lands Act, 1920 for determination as to who were the persons having title to it. The reference, originally registered as Title Suit No. 56 of 1954 was, on transfer, renumbered as Title Suit No. 66 of 1957 of the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal. Government was one of the claimants. Government claimed that this Mouza Rupapura Sonapura appertained to Touzi No. 5077 of Bakerganj Collectorate. It was contended that though the original land appertained to Touzi No. 1566 of Noakhali Collectorate it was transferred to Bakerganj Collectorate in 1865 and was assigned Touzi No. 5077. For default in payment of revenue, it was purchased by Government on March 24, 1875, whereupon all subordinate interests were annulled and it was under periodical settlements with different persons till it was completely diluviated in 1894. It reappeared and reformed in situ in 1947-48. The appellants before us were claimants of Group 'B' of the reference case. Their case was that inspite of its transfer from Noakhali to Bakerganj Collectorate this mouza retained the original Touzi No. 1566 and claimants had their mirash ejara right in the mouza at a jama of Tk. 82-4-0 annas. They contended that this mouza was not auction purchased by the Government in the year 1875 and the land purchased by the Collector in auction bears Touzi No. 5077. The claimants of Group 'B' filed a suit in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court Barisal, being numbered as Title Suit No. 47 of 1950 of that Court. This Suit, on transfer to the local third Court of Sub ordinate Judge, was renumbered as Title Suit No. 26 of 1954. Both the reference and the suit were tried together. The trial Court decreed the Title Suit No. 66 of 1957 in favour of the Government and dismissed the Title Suit No. 26 of 1954 brought by the claimants of Group 'B'. First Appeal Nos. 119 and 120 of 1951 arose and in appeal the High Court Division accepted the contention of the claimants of Group 'B', the appellants before us and rejected and reference of the Collector. The High Court Division found that the land of the suit belonging to mouza Rupapura Sonapura bearing Revenue Survey No. 1547 appertained to Touzi No. 1566 and was not auction sold and purchased by the Collector as alleged by the Government. The High Court Division further found that government had auction purchased Touzi No. 5077 of Bakerganj Collectorate which was a Touzi different from Touzi No. 1566 originally of Noakhali Collectorate and subsequently transferred to Bakerganj Collectorate and the land of the suit did not appertain to that Touzi purchased by the Government. The Division Bench found title of the disputed land in the appellants before us and decreed their suit. Leave to appeal before the Appellate Division was refused. Thereafter the plaintiffs have brought the present suit for declaration of their title claiming title on the strength of raiyati settlements between the years 1958-1959, 1959-60 and 1960-61. The plaintiffs alleged. that the defendants-appellants and their co-sharers on suppression of facts and without affording opportunity to the Revenue Officer of the Government secured the decree in the first appeal from the High Court Division and that they being raiyats under the Government for more than 12 years Were not liable to be evicted.
